    14→// This creates a custom HTTP transport which we can attach to our HTTP client
    15→// in order to inject JWT auth strings into our HTTP request headers. Authentication
    16→// is required when interacting with an Ethereum engine API server via HTTP, and JWT
    17→// is chosen as the scheme of choice.

    19→// the specification here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/authentication.md
    20→//
    21→// To use this transport, initialize a new &http.Client{} from the standard library
    22→// and set the Transport field to &jwtTransport{} with values
    23→// http.DefaultTransport and a JWT secret.
    24→type jwtTransport struct {
    25→	underlyingTransport http.RoundTripper
    26→	jwtSecret           []byte
    27→	jwtId               string
    28→}
    29→
    30→// RoundTrip ensures our transport implements http.RoundTripper interface from the
    31→// standard library. When used as the transport for an HTTP client, the code below
    32→// will run every time our client makes an HTTP request. This is used to inject
    33→// an JWT bearer token in the Authorization request header of every outgoing request
    34→// our HTTP client makes.
    35→func (t *jwtTransport) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
    36→	claims := jwt.MapClaims{
    37→		// Required claim for engine API auth. "iat" stands for issued at
    38→		// and it must be a unix timestamp that is +/- 5 seconds from the current
    39→		// timestamp at the moment the server verifies this value.
    40→		"iat": time.Now().Unix(),
    41→	}
    42→	if len(t.jwtId) > 0 {
    43→		claims["id"] = t.jwtId
    44→	}
    45→	token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, claims)
    46→	tokenString, err := token.SignedString(t.jwtSecret)
    47→	if err != nil {
    48→		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "could not produce signed JWT token")
    49→	}
    50→	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+tokenString)
    51→	return t.underlyingTransport.RoundTrip(req)
    52→}
